This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building nonparametric methods — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary nonparametric methods tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple nonparametric methods strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Validate nonparametric methods outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
3. Keep nonparametric methods changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. State assumptions about nonparametric methods explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
5. Re-check edge cases relevant to nonparametric methods (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
6. Before starting nonparametric methods work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
7. When nonparametric methods decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Keep nonparametric methods outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
9. Measure before optimizing any nonparametric methods bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
10. Prefer explicit, readable nonparametric methods solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new nonparametric methods abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting nonparametric methods assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of nonparametric methods correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated nonparametric methods concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for nonparametric methods, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
